sections.html:
Oklahoma evictions run through a court case named Forcible Entry and Detainer, shortened to FED. No one but a judge can order a tenant to leave. Changing the locks, or cutting water, heat, electricity or gas, is off limits to the landlord even if the tenant owes rent.

Small claims court hears most residential cases. The landlord typically asks for possession of the house, a money judgment for unpaid rent and damage, or both.

Selling a rented house does not stop or replace the case. Its pace comes from the tenant's notice dates and the court calendar. Your closing date has no say.

Each reason for removal has its own clock under Title 41. Landlords often lose ground right here, by filing in court without the matching notice.

Written notice by eviction reason
SituationNotice or time period
Rent not paidFive days from written demand, which also serves as the demand for possession (41 O.S. 131(B))
Breach the tenant can fixWritten notice giving 10 days to fix it, with the tenancy ending 15 days after receipt if not fixed (41 O.S. 132(B))
Month-to-month or at-will tenancyWritten notice of 30 days, from landlord or tenant (41 O.S. 111)
Tenancy shorter than month-to-monthWritten notice of 7 days (41 O.S. 111)
Fire, flood or similar emergency caused by tenant24 to 48 hours written notice
Drug-related or threatening crime24 hour written notice

When a lease has a set end date, it lapses on that date by itself unless the parties agreed otherwise.

Handing the paper to the tenant is the preferred method when the tenant can be found. Section 111 gives two fallbacks: delivery to a family member over twelve who lives with the tenant, and then posting on the door plus a mailed copy.

  • First choice: personal delivery to the tenant.
  • Second: a family member over age twelve living there.
  • Third: a copy posted in a visible spot on the home, with another copy mailed by certified mail or the Postal Service accountable mail book.

In plain terms there are two routes, post it and mail it, or hand it over through the landlord, a process server or the sheriff.

sections.h2: How quickly the case moves once filed
sections.html:
Very quickly. The summons under 12 O.S. 1148.4 puts the trial 5 to 10 days out from issuance and must spell out the claim plus the sum the landlord will take if the tenant stays away.

Section 1148.5 of Title 12 requires service no later than three days before trial. If reasonable efforts at hand delivery fail, the statute allows leaving a copy with a resident over fifteen at the home, or sending certified mail postmarked at least three days before trial.

A tenant who does not show up may lose by default, meaning the landlord wins without argument.

sections.h2: When the judge sides with the landlord
sections.html:
With a possession judgment in hand, the landlord requests a writ of execution from the court clerk, and the sheriff or another officer enforces it. Under 12 O.S. 1148.10 the writ directs removal of the defendant, return of possession to the plaintiff and collection of rent, fees and costs.

  • Any motion for new trial is due in three days, and it leaves the writ in force.
  • Under 12 O.S. 1148.10A the officer or landlord warns the tenant of a return in 48 hours, either in person or by a posted notice.
  • Refusing to leave once the writ is served is a trespass offense carrying a fine of up to $500, up to 30 days in county jail, or both.
  • To appeal, the tenant may post a supersedeas bond within 2 days of judgment, which a judge can extend to no more than 7 days, and must keep paying current rent into the court clerk's office.

Missing a rent payment during an appeal is treated as giving up the appeal.

Wrongfully removing or shutting out a tenant is costly. Section 123 of Title 41 lets the tenant retake possession or cancel the rental agreement, and in both cases collect the larger of twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages.

If the tenant ends the rental, the landlord must also return recoverable deposits and prepaid rent. A seller who locks a tenant out to clear the house for a buyer ends up with a larger problem than the one being solved.

Section 130 of Title 41 covers both abandonment and lawful removal after an eviction. Items the landlord judges to have no apparent value may be disposed of, with no duty to account for them.

Items that do appear valuable require a written notice by certified mail to the tenant's last known address. Property left with the landlord for 30 days or longer is conclusively treated as abandoned. The landlord must store items safely and use reasonable care, and may charge storage costs.

When a tenant who was the only occupant dies, 41 O.S. 130.1 sets a separate process for a designated contact, including a 30 day mailed request before property is discarded.

Selling does not terminate the tenancy. Section 119 of Title 41 makes the landlord's conveyance valid with no need for the tenant to agree, and rent paid to the seller before written notice of the sale reaches the tenant counts as properly paid.

After written notice, rent goes to the buyer. The seller is freed from duties for anything after that point, and the successor steps into the obligations of the rental agreement.

Showings are permitted within limits. Section 128 lets a landlord bring prospective buyers in with a day's notice, at reasonable times, unless an emergency exists.

sections.h2: What rental owners commonly run into
sections.html:
A case is filed where the house sits, so you will deal with that county's clerk and calendar. Typical snags:

  • A month-to-month tenant is owed a full 30 days of written notice, which may run longer than a buyer's closing window.
  • A tenant who is behind can remain through hearing and appeal by paying rent into court.
  • Property left behind after a hearing means more time and storage duties.
  • A damaged rental can raise habitability disputes before any eviction starts.

Some owners skip all this by selling as is with the tenant in place, so the buyer takes over the lease and whatever is on the court calendar.

faqs.q: How many days does an Oklahoma landlord have to give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Five days from the written demand. When the tenant has not paid by then, 41 O.S. 131(B) lets the landlord terminate the agreement, and the same demand counts as the demand for possession.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant without going to court?
faqs.a: No. A judge alone can order a tenant out. A tenant locked out illegally can claim up to twice the monthly rent or twice actual damages under 41 O.S. 123, whichever is higher.

faqs.q: How long does an Oklahoma eviction case take, and can the tenant appeal?
faqs.a: Trial lands 5 to 10 days after the summons issues (12 O.S. 1148.4). A tenant can appeal by posting a supersedeas bond within 2 days, extendable to no more than 7, and must keep paying current rent into court.

faqs.q: Does selling a rented house in Oklahoma cancel the lease?
faqs.a: No. The sale stands without the tenant's consent (41 O.S. 119). The buyer inherits the landlord's duties, and once the tenant is told in writing, rent goes to the buyer.

faqs.q: Can a landlord show a rented house to buyers?
faqs.a: Yes, if the landlord gives a day's notice and comes at a reasonable hour, except in an emergency. Section 128 says the tenant cannot unreasonably refuse entry for showings.
